results.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: OpenAI's New A.I. Models, No. 2 on Artificial Analysis, Pricing and What OpenAI Promises
results.content:
According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2 Astra is its new frontier model for the hardest projects, while GPT-6.2 Sol is the efficient model for everyday work. Both are designed to handle demanding tasks better while using fewer output tokens. They are available now to paying users of ChatGPT Work and Codex, as well as through the API.

## Second Place on Artificial Analysis [...] - Coding: On the Coding Agent Index, Astra is flat, and Sol even loses three points. The reason is a 14-point drop on SWE-Atlas-QnA, where Sol is more likely than its predecessor to omit key facts in its responses. Thanks to their low cost, however, several effort levels of Astra and Sol still land on the Pareto frontier. [...] The update is not free of setbacks. In two tests, the new models were more likely to keep quiet about obstacles blocking their work, such as a missing file. According to the system card, Astra did so in about 22 percent of cases, twice as often as GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI has added instructions in Codex that are meant to substantially reduce this, but they do not apply to direct API use.

results.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Sol At DevDay - Dataconomy
results.content:
OpenAI said the new model is more direct about its limitations and more reliable in following user intent and safety constraints. In internal evaluations, the company said GPT-6.1 Sol failed less often than GPT-6 Sol when identifying broken search tools, following explicit restrictions and avoiding unauthorized outcomes during tasks.

OpenAI said it observed no attempts by GPT-6.1 Sol to bypass the automated safety reviewer, matching the behavior it reported for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol. [...] OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol at its DevDay event on Tuesday, saying the model delivers near GPT-6 Astra-level performance for coding and professional tasks at one-fifth of the standard token price.

The company did not release GPT-6.1 Astra, which had been expected. The Wall Street Journal reported this week that OpenAI scrapped the launch after internal testing raised safety concerns about higher levels of deception and a tendency to continue tasks without user permission. [...] OpenAI also said GPT-6.1 Sol improves factual accuracy on difficult prompts. At low reasoning effort, the share of responses containing a factual error fell to 7.7% from 11.4% for GPT-6 Sol.

Across all reasoning settings, GPT-6.1 Sol’s error rate remains within 1.9% of GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI said.

results.title: OpenAI model release dates: o3, GPT-5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna in order · Think Facility
results.content:
## Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna: which GPT is which

This is the part that confused me. In July, OpenAI stopped using plain version numbers and gave the GPT-5.6 family three names: Sol "for frontier capability", Terra "for a balance of intelligence and cost" and Luna "for efficient, high-volume workloads". Sol was the top. [...] GPT-6 kept two of those names and moved one of them. Astra is the new top, and the models page now says to use it if you're "not sure where to start". GPT-6 Sol is the middle model, there to "balance intelligence and cost", which is the job Terra had. Luna is still the cheap one. There's no GPT-6 Terra on the page at all. [...] That makes "Sol" ambiguous. GPT-5.6 Sol is last generation's flagship and GPT-6 Sol is this generation's mid-tier. They're separate models with separate IDs (`gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6-sol`), so check which one a benchmark or a forum post means before you compare anything.

| Model | Role | In / out per 1M |
 --- 
| GPT-6 Astra | Flagship | $10 / $50 |
| GPT-6 Sol | Middle | $2 / $10 |
| GPT-6 Luna | Cheap, high volume | $0.10 / $0.50 |
| GPT-5.6 Sol | Last generation's top | $4 / $20 |

results.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna | OpenAI
results.content:
That’s why we’re expanding the GPT‑6 universe with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna.GPT‑6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence—these models help distribute the benefits of that intelligence by advancing the frontier on cost efficiency. We trained GPT‑6 Sol and Luna with similar methods as GPT‑6 Astra, bringing the advances behind Astra’s state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable models. [...] ### Computer use

While GPT‑6 Astra remains the world’s best model for computer use, GPT‑6 Sol and Luna offer more cost-efficient performance than their predecessors. On OSWorld 2.0 offline, GPT‑6 Sol at xhigh effort achieves a similar score to Claude Opus 5 at medium effort—60.5% versus 60.3%—at approximately 80% lower cost per task. GPT‑6 Luna (max) is able to exceed GPT‑5.6 Sol (medium) at one tenth of its cost. [...] GPT‑6 Sol and Luna build on the alignment work introduced with Astra, our most aligned model to date. In our alignment evaluations, both Sol and Luna show improvements over their GPT‑5.6 counterparts, including lower rates of misleading claims about their coding work.

The evaluations below deliberately test challenging situations and do not measure failure rates in typical use. See the system card⁠(opens in a new window) for the full results.
